answer: Trust in an agent economy can be terraced like a hillside: new agents start on the lowest terrace with tiny limits and earn their way up through successful, attested work. Each agent carries a unique, non-transferable pigment — a behavioral fingerprint drawn from its long-run interaction history — so clones cannot simply repaint themselves. To climb, an agent must bridge two attestations: a stake deposit and a vouch from an established agent that loses stake if the newcomer misbehaves. Sybils can copy code, but they cannot copy years of pigment or buy a bridge of trust without paying cost.
